questionText:
Read the following excerpt carefully and answer the question that follows:

"A peasant cultivator named Vithoba from Poona district gave the following testimony before the Deccan Riots Commission in 1876: 'I borrowed Rs. 50 from the Marwari sahukar seven years ago during a drought. I have repaid him more than Rs. 150 in grain and cash over the years. Yet, whenever I ask for my bond back, he claims that the interest has accumulated to Rs. 300. He never gives me a receipt for the grain I deliver. Three years ago, he forced me to sign a blank piece of paper with a stamp on it, saying that under the new Limitation Law of 1859 the old bond had expired. He threatened that if I did not sign, he would obtain a decree from the civil court and auction my bullocks and ancestral land.
